q: The state of the art of chemistry lies on the chemical calculations, which are mainly based on the quantities of chemical terms (especially the chemical symbol and the ____) and other relevant data.
e: The state of the art of chemistry lies on the chemical calculations, which are mainly based on the quantities of chemical terms (especially the chemical symbol and the Mole) and other relevant data. The mole is the chemist's counting unit, tied to 6.02 x 10^23 particles.

q: Atoms and molecules are particles that make up ____.
e: Atoms and molecules are particles that make up matter. Matter is the idea that completes this fact.

q: However, in chemical calculations, chemists use relative masses of atoms and molecules on the basis of a designated standard unit mass, called ____.
e: However, in chemical calculations, chemists use relative masses of atoms and molecules on the basis of a designated standard unit mass, called atomic mass unit (amu). Atomic mass unit (amu) is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Atoms of different elements have different ____.
e: Atoms of different elements have different masses. Masses is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The mass of a single atom is so small that it is impossible to weigh it ____.
e: The mass of a single atom is so small that it is impossible to weigh it directly. Directly is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Now, scientists have chosen to use the isotope ____ as the new standard because it is the most abundant isotope.
e: Now, scientists have chosen to use the isotope carbon-12 as the new standard because it is the most abundant isotope. Carbon-12 is the mass standard: one-twelfth of that atom is the atomic mass unit.

q: The mass of an atom is called its ____.
e: The mass of an atom is called its atomic mass. Atomic mass is the idea that completes this fact.

q: For the fact that the size of an atom is too small to be weighed practically, ____ is therefore used to represent the mass of an atom of an element.
e: For the fact that the size of an atom is too small to be weighed practically, relative atomic mass is therefore used to represent the mass of an atom of an element. Relative atomic mass compares the average atom of an element with one-twelfth of carbon-12.

q: Thus, the relative atomic mass of an element is the average mass of one atom of the element compared with ____ the mass of one atom of the carbon-12 ($^{12}C$) isotope whose mass is exactly 12.
e: Thus, the relative atomic mass of an element is the average mass of one atom of the element compared with one twelfth the mass of one atom of the carbon-12 (12C) isotope whose mass is exactly 12. Carbon-12 is the mass standard: one-twelfth of that atom is the atomic mass unit. Relative atomic mass compares the average atom of an element with one-twelfth of carbon-12.

q: Atomic mass unit (amu) is precisely ____ the mass of one atom of carbon-12.
e: Atomic mass unit (amu) is precisely one twelfth the mass of one atom of carbon-12. Carbon-12 is the mass standard: one-twelfth of that atom is the atomic mass unit.

q: To calculate the relative atomic mass of an element, we must know the isotopic masses and the relative ____ of the isotopes in nature.
e: To calculate the relative atomic mass of an element, we must know the isotopic masses and the relative abundance of the isotopes in nature. Abundance is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The ____ of a molecule is the mass of one molecule of a substance on a scale where the carbon-12 isotopes has a mass of exactly 12 units (12 amu).
e: The relative molecular mass of a molecule is the mass of one molecule of a substance on a scale where the carbon-12 isotopes has a mass of exactly 12 units (12 amu). Relative molecular mass is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Thus, the relative molecular mass ($M_r$) can be found by adding up the relative ____ of all the atoms present in the molecule.
e: Thus, the relative molecular mass (M_r) can be found by adding up the relative atomic masses of all the atoms present in the molecule. Atomic masses is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Ionic compounds, such as sodium chloride and magnesium oxide consist of ions and not ____.
e: Ionic compounds, such as sodium chloride and magnesium oxide consist of ions and not molecules. Molecules is the idea that completes this fact.

q: For ionic compounds, we use the term ____ instead of relative molecular mass.
e: For ionic compounds, we use the term relative formula mass instead of relative molecular mass. Relative formula mass is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Every compound has a formula as well as a ____.
e: Every compound has a formula as well as a name. Name is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The formula is made up of the ____ for the elements.
e: The formula is made up of the symbols for the elements. Symbols is the idea that completes this fact.

q: A symbol is a shorthand notation of an ____.
e: A symbol is a shorthand notation of an element. An element is a substance made of only one kind of atom.

q: The first letter in the name of an element is usually chosen as the ____ of the element.
e: The first letter in the name of an element is usually chosen as the symbol of the element. Symbol is the idea that completes this fact.

q: A symbol represents an atom of the element and the ____ of an atom.
e: A symbol represents an atom of the element and the mass of an atom. Mass is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The symbols of some other elements, which have been known since earlier times, are taken from ____ names.
e: The symbols of some other elements, which have been known since earlier times, are taken from Latin names. Latin is the idea that completes this fact.

q: A ____ is a shorthand notation representing a molecule or a compound of a substance.
e: A molecular formula is a shorthand notation representing a molecule or a compound of a substance. A molecular formula shows the actual number of each atom in a molecule.

q: A molecular formula shows the number of ____ contained in a molecule or a compound.
e: A molecular formula shows the number of atoms contained in a molecule or a compound. Atoms is the idea that completes this fact.

q: For those compounds which exist in the form of giant structure, a formula represents the simplest ____ of the compound.
e: For those compounds which exist in the form of giant structure, a formula represents the simplest unit of the compound. Unit is the idea that completes this fact.

q: As compounds of giant structure do not have separate molecules, they cannot have molecular mass, so ____ mass is used instead.
e: As compounds of giant structure do not have separate molecules, they cannot have molecular mass, so formula mass is used instead. A molecular formula shows the actual number of each atom in a molecule.

q: The first step in identifying a chemical formula is to find out its ____ formula.
e: The first step in identifying a chemical formula is to find out its empirical formula. An empirical formula is the simplest whole-number ratio of atoms in a compound.

q: The empirical formula of a compound is the ____ formula of the compound.
e: The empirical formula of a compound is the simplest formula of the compound. An empirical formula is the simplest whole-number ratio of atoms in a compound.

q: The empirical formula shows the types of elements present and the simplest ____ of the different types of the atoms in the compound.
e: The empirical formula shows the types of elements present and the simplest ratio of the different types of the atoms in the compound. An empirical formula is the simplest whole-number ratio of atoms in a compound.

q: An empirical formula can also be deduced from data that give the percentage composition by ____ of the elements in a compound.
e: An empirical formula can also be deduced from data that give the percentage composition by mass of the elements in a compound. Mass is the idea that completes this fact.

q: For some compounds such as magnesium oxide, the empirical formula accurately shows the number of atoms in the compound, but the actual formula is called the ____ formula.
e: For some compounds such as magnesium oxide, the empirical formula accurately shows the number of atoms in the compound, but the actual formula is called the molecular formula. A molecular formula shows the actual number of each atom in a molecule.

q: We call the actual formula of a compound the ____ formula.
e: We call the actual formula of a compound the molecular formula. A molecular formula shows the actual number of each atom in a molecule.

q: When the empirical and molecular formulae of a compound are different, the molecular formula is always a ____ of the empirical formula.
e: When the empirical and molecular formulae of a compound are different, the molecular formula is always a multiple of the empirical formula. Multiple is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The formula of a compound and relative atomic masses can be used to calculate the percentage by ____ of a particular element in a compound.
e: The formula of a compound and relative atomic masses can be used to calculate the percentage by mass of a particular element in a compound. Relative atomic mass compares the average atom of an element with one-twelfth of carbon-12.

q: The combining capacity or valence of an element is represented by the number of atoms of hydrogen, chlorine or sodium that combine with ____ atom of that element.
e: The combining capacity or valence of an element is represented by the number of atoms of hydrogen, chlorine or sodium that combine with one atom of that element. One is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The term '____' is also used to express combining capacity.
e: The term 'valence' is also used to express combining capacity. Valence tells how many electrons an atom typically uses in bonding.

q: ____ describes the combining capacity of the element and also indicates the positive and negative nature of its atoms in the compounds.
e: Oxidation number describes the combining capacity of the element and also indicates the positive and negative nature of its atoms in the compounds. Oxidation number is a bookkeeping charge that tracks electron transfer.

q: The oxidation number is related to, but not identical with valence or combining ____.
e: The oxidation number is related to, but not identical with valence or combining capacity. Capacity is the idea that completes this fact.

q: In the compounds formed by the combination of metals with non-metals, metals always show ____ character.
e: In the compounds formed by the combination of metals with non-metals, metals always show electropositive character. Electropositive is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The combining capacities of metals in most cases are expressed by using ____ oxidation numbers.
e: The combining capacities of metals in most cases are expressed by using positive oxidation numbers. Positive is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The combining capacities of the non-metallic elements are expressed by using ____ oxidation numbers.
e: The combining capacities of the non-metallic elements are expressed by using negative oxidation numbers. Negative is the idea that completes this fact.

q: In compounds formed by the combination of one non-metal with another, the more ____ element is assigned a positive oxidation number and the other is assigned a negative oxidation number.
e: In compounds formed by the combination of one non-metal with another, the more electropositive element is assigned a positive oxidation number and the other is assigned a negative oxidation number. Electropositive is the idea that completes this fact.

q: A binary compound is a compound which contains ____ elements only.
e: A binary compound is a compound which contains two elements only. Two is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Metallic binary compounds contain a metal, and non metallic binary compounds contain ____ elements only.
e: Metallic binary compounds contain a metal, and non metallic binary compounds contain non-metallic elements only. Non-metallic is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The more electropositive element present in the compound with positive oxidation number is written in ____ of the symbol of the element with negative oxidation number.
e: The more electropositive element present in the compound with positive oxidation number is written in front of the symbol of the element with negative oxidation number. Front is the idea that completes this fact.

q: One exception is $NH_3$ in which the symbol of the element with ____ oxidation number (N) is written first.
e: One exception is NH3 in which the symbol of the element with negative oxidation number (N) is written first. Negative is the idea that completes this fact.

q: In the formula of a compound, the algebraic sum of the oxidation numbers must be equal to ____.
e: In the formula of a compound, the algebraic sum of the oxidation numbers must be equal to zero. Zero is the idea that completes this fact.

q: For the naming of non-metallic binary compounds, ____ prefixes (e.g., mono-, di-, tri-, etc.) are used to indicate the number of atoms of each element in the compound.
e: For the naming of non-metallic binary compounds, Greek prefixes (e.g., mono-, di-, tri-, etc.) are used to indicate the number of atoms of each element in the compound. Greek is the idea that completes this fact.

q: In those cases where there is only one atom of the first element, the use of the prefix ____ is not necessary.
e: In those cases where there is only one atom of the first element, the use of the prefix mono is not necessary. Mono is the idea that completes this fact.

q: For naming the metallic binary compounds, the name of the more electropositive metallic element with variable oxidation number is given first, followed by the ____ in brackets to state its oxidation number.
e: For naming the metallic binary compounds, the name of the more electropositive metallic element with variable oxidation number is given first, followed by the Roman Numeral in brackets to state its oxidation number. Roman Numeral is the idea that completes this fact.

q: When H is removed from the formula of HCl, the remaining part is -Cl, which represents the ____ radical of hydrochloric acid.
e: When H is removed from the formula of HCl, the remaining part is -Cl, which represents the acid radical of hydrochloric acid. Acid is the idea that completes this fact.

q: In naming the acids which have hydrogen atoms in their molecules the name of acid radical -ic is changed to ____.
e: In naming the acids which have hydrogen atoms in their molecules the name of acid radical -ic is changed to -ide. -ide is the idea that completes this fact.

q: In naming the acids which have oxygen atoms in their molecules the names of the acid radicals are as follows: -ous acid becomes ____.
e: In naming the acids which have oxygen atoms in their molecules the names of the acid radicals are as follows: -ous acid becomes -ite. -ite is the idea that completes this fact.

q: In naming the acids which have oxygen atoms in their molecules the names of the acid radicals are as follows: -ic acid becomes ____.
e: In naming the acids which have oxygen atoms in their molecules the names of the acid radicals are as follows: -ic acid becomes -ate. -ate is the idea that completes this fact.

q: In naming the acid radicals containing H, the word ____ is placed before the name of the acid radical.
e: In naming the acid radicals containing H, the word hydrogen is placed before the name of the acid radical. Hydrogen is the lightest element and a common fuel and reducing agent in the lab.

q: The ion formed after removal of hydroxide ions ($OH^-$ ions) from a base is called ____ radical.
e: The ion formed after removal of hydroxide ions (OH- ions) from a base is called basic radical. Basic is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The formula of a salt consists of ____ parts.
e: The formula of a salt consists of two parts. Two is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The first part of a salt formula is the metal atom or the ____ radical.
e: The first part of a salt formula is the metal atom or the ammonium radical. Ammonium is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The second part of a salt formula is the ____ radical.
e: The second part of a salt formula is the acid radical. Acid is the idea that completes this fact.

q: When writing the formula of a salt, the algebraic sum of the oxidation numbers must be equal to ____.
e: When writing the formula of a salt, the algebraic sum of the oxidation numbers must be equal to zero. Zero is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The name of the salt begins with the name of the metal or ammonium radical, followed by the name of the ____ radical.
e: The name of the salt begins with the name of the metal or ammonium radical, followed by the name of the acid radical. Acid is the idea that completes this fact.

q: All hydroxides include one or more -OH radicals of oxidation number ____ in their formulae.
e: All hydroxides include one or more -OH radicals of oxidation number -1 in their formulae. -1 is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Hydroxides are named in the same way as the naming of salts, but the name of acid radical is replaced by the word ____.
e: Hydroxides are named in the same way as the naming of salts, but the name of acid radical is replaced by the word hydroxide. Hydroxide is the idea that completes this fact.

q: An important use of empirical formula calculation is in ____ chemistry, where almost every day a new compound is discovered or made.
e: An important use of empirical formula calculation is in organic chemistry, where almost every day a new compound is discovered or made. Organic chemistry studies carbon compounds, especially hydrocarbons and their derivatives.

q: Sodium hydrogen carbonate ($NaHCO_3$), is used in the manufacture of some toothpaste and as a raising agent in ____ production.
e: Sodium hydrogen carbonate (NaHCO3), is used in the manufacture of some toothpaste and as a raising agent in food production. Plant breeding, pest control, and other biological work have raised how much food we can grow.

q: An important element for the growth of plants is ____.
e: An important element for the growth of plants is nitrogen. Nitrogen is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The relative atomic masses of elements expressed in amu are not feasible to be used in the weighable scale, especially in ____.
e: The relative atomic masses of elements expressed in amu are not feasible to be used in the weighable scale, especially in grams. Grams is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The chemists' counting unit is named the ____, and it is defined as equal to the number of atoms in exactly 12 g of $^{12}C$.
e: The chemists' counting unit is named the mole, and it is defined as equal to the number of atoms in exactly 12 g of 12C. The mole is the chemist's counting unit, tied to 6.02 x 10^23 particles.

q: This number of particles is called Avogadro's ____, which is equal to $6.02 imes 10^{23}$.
e: This number of particles is called Avogadro's constant, which is equal to 6.02 imes 1023. Constant is the idea that completes this fact.

q: We may refer to the mass of a mole of substance as its ____ mass.
e: We may refer to the mass of a mole of substance as its molar mass. Molar mass is the mass of one mole of a substance, in grams per mole.

q: The unit of molar mass is ____.
e: The unit of molar mass is g mol-1. G mol-1 is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Molar mass is the relative atomic, molecular or formula mass of the substance in ____.
e: Molar mass is the relative atomic, molecular or formula mass of the substance in grams. Grams is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The number of atoms in a mole of atoms is very large: $6.02 imes 10^{23}$ atoms, and this number is called the Avogadro's constant or Avogadro's ____.
e: The number of atoms in a mole of atoms is very large: 6.02 imes 1023 atoms, and this number is called the Avogadro's constant or Avogadro's number. Number is the idea that completes this fact.

q: One mole of a substance is the amount of substance that has the same number of particles (atoms, molecules, etc.) as there are atoms in exactly ____ g of $^{12}C$.
e: One mole of a substance is the amount of substance that has the same number of particles (atoms, molecules, etc.) as there are atoms in exactly 12 g of 12C. Carbon-12 is the mass standard: one-twelfth of that atom is the atomic mass unit.

q: The Avogadro's constant applies to atoms, molecules, ____ and electrons.
e: The Avogadro's constant applies to atoms, molecules, ions and electrons. Ions is the idea that completes this fact.

q: In 1 mole of sodium chloride (NaCl) there are $6.02 imes 10^{23}$ sodium ions and $6.02 imes 10^{23}$ ____ ions.
e: In 1 mole of sodium chloride (NaCl) there are 6.02 imes 1023 sodium ions and 6.02 imes 1023 chloride ions. Chloride is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Amedeo Avogadro was an Italian scientist who first deduced that ____ of gases contain equal number of molecules under the same conditions of temperature and pressure.
e: Amedeo Avogadro was an Italian scientist who first deduced that equal volumes of gases contain equal number of molecules under the same conditions of temperature and pressure. Equal volumes is the idea that completes this fact.

q: One mole of any gas has a volume of ____ or $24,000 cm^3$ at room temperature and pressure (r.t.p.).
e: One mole of any gas has a volume of 24 dm3 or 24,000 cm3 at room temperature and pressure (r.t.p.). 24 dm3 is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The volume of one mole of any gas at room temperature and pressure is called the ____ volume of a gas.
e: The volume of one mole of any gas at room temperature and pressure is called the molar volume of a gas. Molar is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Room temperature and pressure are often taken as conditions of ____ and 1 atmosphere.
e: Room temperature and pressure are often taken as conditions of 25 degrees C and 1 atmosphere. 25 degrees C is the idea that completes this fact.

q: To convert volumes of gases into moles, the volume of the gas is divided by the ____ volume of the gas at r.t.p.
e: To convert volumes of gases into moles, the volume of the gas is divided by the molar volume of the gas at r.t.p. Molar is the idea that completes this fact.

q: One mole of every gas occupies ____ at STP (standard temperature, $0^{\circ} C$ or 273 K and standard pressure, 760 mmHg or 1 atmosphere).
e: One mole of every gas occupies 22.4 dm3 at STP (standard temperature, 0 degrees C or 273 K and standard pressure, 760 mmHg or 1 atmosphere). 22.4 dm3 is the idea that completes this fact.

q: STP stands for standard temperature and ____.
e: STP stands for standard temperature and pressure. Raising temperature or lowering pressure helps a liquid evaporate.

q: The Systeme International (SI) unit for mass is the ____.
e: The Systeme International (SI) unit for mass is the kilogram. Kilogram is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Chemists prefer to use the relative molecular mass or formula mass in grams because the kilogram is a rather ____ mass to use for general laboratory work.
e: Chemists prefer to use the relative molecular mass or formula mass in grams because the kilogram is a rather large mass to use for general laboratory work. Large is the idea that completes this fact.

q: You can find the number of moles of a substance by dividing the mass of substance by its ____ mass.
e: You can find the number of moles of a substance by dividing the mass of substance by its molar mass. Molar mass is the mass of one mole of a substance, in grams per mole.

q: To find the mass of a substance present in a given number of moles, you multiply the number of moles by the ____ mass.
e: To find the mass of a substance present in a given number of moles, you multiply the number of moles by the molar mass. Molar mass is the mass of one mole of a substance, in grams per mole.

q: In order to make a drug from its ingredients, someone has to figure out how much of each ingredient is needed to react together, which involves using the concept of ____.
e: In order to make a drug from its ingredients, someone has to figure out how much of each ingredient is needed to react together, which involves using the concept of moles. The mole is the chemist's counting unit, tied to 6.02 x 10^23 particles.

q: In combustion, you need to use mole to know how much ____ is needed and how much exhaust would be produced.
e: In combustion, you need to use mole to know how much air is needed and how much exhaust would be produced. Air is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Chemicals in batteries react to produce ____, and people have to figure out the amount of moles of each reactant needed.
e: Chemicals in batteries react to produce electricity, and people have to figure out the amount of moles of each reactant needed. Electricity is the idea that completes this fact.
